title: SOC2 prep scratchpad - grace lin
content:
SOC2 prep scratchpad - Grace

Quick context: pulling together notes for control mapping and answering preliminary auditor risk questions. This is messy - notes to self and stuff to hand off to Maya/Ryan for review.

Top priorities:
- map existing controls to Trust Service Criteria (TSC) 2024 version. focus: CC, CC2 (change mgmt), CC6 (access), PI (privacy) for now
- gather evidence for last 12 months (logs, runbooks, incident postmortems, IAM lists)
- draft responses for auditor risk questionnaire (initial pass)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Backup retention policy: where is the written policy? I think infra has a page but need formal doc id. TODO: ask infra (Oliver Park).
- Encryption at rest: we use KMS keys in prod, but need inventory of keys and who has admin access (KMS admins). Is there a key-rotation log?
- Third-party vendors: need updated vendor inventory and SOC2 status for each (Sentry, Segment, Logflare?). Quick list to confirm: Sentry (?), Datadog (has SOC2), Segment (?), Auth0(?) - verify.

Control mapping notes (rough):
- CC6 (logical access):
  - Controls: IAM role review quarterly (owner: eng-sre). Evidence: quarterly access review spreadsheet, Okta reports.
  - Gap: proof of enforcement for service accounts older than 90 days. Action: run script to list stale service accounts (SEC-201).

- CC2 (change mgmt):
  - Controls: PR review policy for prod; release checklist in GitHub; rollout / canary notes in Console. Evidence: sample PRs, release notes, runbook entry for rollback.
  - Gap: emergency change logging - need to capture post-facto approvals in Jira. Suggest small template for emergency changes.

- CC3 (system operations):
  - Controls: incident response runbooks (SRE runbooks in Confluence), pager duty rotations. Evidence: incident postmortems (last 6 months).
  - Gap: formal tabletop exercise schedule - I think we did one in 2024 but need evidence (email invite, deck).

Draft answers for auditor risk questionnaire (first pass):
Q: Describe how access to production systems is controlled and monitored.
A: Access to production systems is centrally managed via Okta SSO and fine-grained IAM roles enforced in cloud provider. Privileged roles are limited to named engineers and require 2FA. Access reviews are performed quarterly by role owners; access removal is automated via offboarding workflow tied to HR signals. Activities in prod are logged to centralized logging (Datadog/Logflare) with retention of 365 days; logs are aggregated and alerts configured for anomalous activity. (Need: link to access review spreadsheet and one sample log export)

Q: How do you prevent unauthorized code changes from reaching production?
A: Code changes require PRs and peer review; CI runs automated tests and static checks. Protected branches + required reviewers for main. Deployments are done through our CI/CD pipeline with approvals for prod environment. Emergency change process requires retrospective approval and a documented rollback plan. (Need: PR examples + pipeline config snippet)

Evidence to collect (short list):
- Okta admin CSV export (current users + last login)
- Quarterly access review spreadsheet (2024-Q1..Q4)
- Sample PR + associated release notes for one rollout in 2024
- Incident postmortems (Jan 2024, Sep 2024, Dec 2024)
- KMS key inventory and rotation logs
- Vendor inventory doc (with vendor SOC2 status)
- Backup policy doc & recent backup test results
- Tabletop exercise deck/email invite

Action items (assign and rough ETA):
- Ask infra (Oliver) for backup policy doc and backup test evidence. owner: Oliver Park. ETA: 2025-02-18.
- Export Okta users and share to auditors (redact PII as needed). owner: Maya Singh. ETA: 2025-02-10.
- Run stale service account report and tidy (script in infra repo). owner: Ryan Chen. ETA: 2025-02-12.
- Draft emergency change template for Jira and link to PRs. owner: Grace Lin. ETA: 2025-02-14.
- Gather incident postmortems and tag relevant controls. owner: SRE (TBD). ETA: 2025-02-21.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally rough. When we hand off to auditors we should package evidence with a little index (spreadsheet mapping control -> artifact file name -> dates).
- For now prioritize access / change mgmt controls - auditors usually focus there first and they unblock a lot of other checks.

Links / refs (working):
- Confluence control matrix: https://confluence.redwood.example/pages/CONF-3245-soc2-control-matrix
- Jira epic: JIRA-SEC-201 (service account cleanup)
- Internal Slack thread: slack://channel/security#thread-abc123

Random brainstorms / future improvements:
- automate control evidence collection: small lambda that pulls logs, access lists, and zips artifacts on demand (could reduce audit prep time from days to hours).
- integrate vendor SOC2 status into vendor onboarding flow so we have status field that is machine-readable.

-- end of scratchpad --

(Will tidy this into a formal control mapping doc once the gaps are closed and the evidence is collected.)
